newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota gov speech pushes transportation, health.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota gov speech pushes transportation, health.

text.p: North Dakota Gov. Edward Schafer outlined what he termed an agressive agenda that emphasized roads, health and international markets in his State of the State Address Monday.

Anticipating fewer federal dollars for road improvements, Schafer called for a state-wide analysis of North Dakota's 107,000 miles of roads to determine which roads are essential to the state's infrastructure.
He also proposed the development of a strategic, proactive health care plan for his state that would include input from health care providers and others.

On the business front, Schafer said the state should "agressively begin competing in national and international markets" by tapping into telecommunications capabilities and possibly creating an export finance program.
Declaring that "North Dakota rocks," Schafer said the state has gained 35,000 new jobs over the past four years, has record- low unemployment levels, and record-high state revenue collections.
Last month, Schafer proposed a $1.94 billion general fund budget for the fiscal 1998-99 bienium. The governor's spending plan included more funding for education and water development.
Schafer, who was relected to a second term as governor Nov. 5, is scheduled to be sworn in Jan. 11.
